relevance_note: Single-patient case report of a girl with SSADHD and a homozygous ALDH5A1 variant: "Molecular testing identified a homozygous ALDH5A1 missense variant".
method_note: One in-scope person, labelled 'patient' (rule 5; the paper uses no own label). Built with a short Python script in the scratch directory; every value was chosen by reading the paper, and spans were located in the paper text (hyphen/quote/thin-space characters matched to the original) and checked verbatim. Relatives not given rows: the parents (described only as reporting symptoms; not tested, not stated affected), 'an intellectual disability in a maternal relative' and 'psychotic illness in paternal relatives' (family history only, unspecified relatives, no testing, not stated to have SSADHD). age_at_last_evaluation records the stated presentation age (12-year-old); the paper reports later longitudinal follow-up without giving an age. Age at onset not recorded: 'At ~3 years of age' is the age at evaluation for developmental delay, not a stated onset; age at diagnosis not stated. Variant: classified by the authors as VUS; 'predicted to be damaging by in silico tools' is not a functional assay, so functional_evidence is not reported. Parental consanguinity stated, but no parental testing, so inheritance not reported. cites_prior_report: the Disclosure says the case was previously mentioned only in abstract/poster form [13]. Not recorded as excluded (hedged or documentation-silence statements): catatonia ('retained in the differential diagnosis but was not favored'), core catatonic signs ('were not prominent'), 'no organized suicidal or violent behavior was documented', disorientation ('not consistently present'), UTI ('did not support'). Negative toxicology, heavy metals, HIV, RPR, hCG results are recorded only here, not as phenotype rows. Checklist: seizures or epilepsy left not reported (only 'No electrographic seizures were recorded' during monitoring, a narrower absence); aggression or disruptive behavior left not reported (agitation and behavioral dysregulation are recorded as features but aggression is not stated); attention problems recorded as observed from impaired attention/distractibility documented during the delirium episode; mood fluctuation observed from 'affective lability'. No contradictions found in the paper. No stacked cells.

treatment_summary.value: Hydroxyzine 25 mg PO every 6 h PRN (six doses HD5 to early HD7, then discontinued); quetiapine 25 mg PO nightly from HD7 plus 12.5 mg PRN on HD8, discharged on quetiapine 25 mg nightly; melatonin; bowel regimen; IV fluids; nonpharmacologic delirium interventions; later as-needed quetiapine and as-needed olanzapine
span: Hydroxyzine was ordered as 25 mg by mouth every 6 h as needed and was administered six times from hospital day 5 through early hospital day 7
Hydroxyzine was discontinued on HD7 because of limited efficacy and concern for the anticholinergic burden
Quetiapine 25 mg by mouth nightly was initiated that evening, and a daytime PRN dose of 12.5 mg was administered on HD8. Melatonin and nonpharmacologic delirium interventions were continued
The patient was discharged on HD10 with quetiapine 25 mg by mouth nightly
was reported to be doing well with as‐needed olanzapine
